description: Preview the first 3 emails of a public Sequenzy email gallery sequence written for this company, without creating a sequence or email (a company's first AI generation saves its inferred email design direction, like generate_email). Each email keeps the example's layout with every word rewritten; returns subject, previewText, HTML and the original day for each, plus how many emails were left out. Pass website to write it for another site's brand instead. Requires sequences:write. Takes 10-30 seconds. Call create_sequence_from_example to create the draft sequence with every email. Accepts a gallery sequence URL or brand plus sequence slugs.

brand.description: Gallery brand slug from the URL (/email-examples/brands/{brand}/...). Use with the example slug instead of url.

brief.description: Optional direction, up to 1000 characters, such as an offer or feature to highlight. Takes priority over the example.

companyId.description: Company ID. If not provided, uses the currently selected company.

sequence.description: Gallery sequence slug from the URL (/sequences/{sequence}). Use with brand instead of url.

url.description: Email gallery page URL. Provide either url, or brand plus the example slug; not both.

website.description: Optional site or domain, like acme.com, to write the preview for instead of this company's own brand.

name: preview_sequence_from_example

outputSchema.description: Structured content returned by the `preview_sequence_from_example` MCP tool.

example.description: The gallery sequence it is modeled on: brand, name, emailCount and url.

items.description: Fallback array wrapper used only when a tool returns a bare array.

message.description: That nothing was saved, and how to clone it.

preview.description: The unsaved rewrite: brandName, website (null for this company's own brand), emails (stepNumber, day, originalSubject, subject, previewText, html for each of the first emails), remainingEmailCount and failedEmailCount.

value.description: Fallback object wrapper used only when a tool returns a non-object value.

warnings.description: Non-fatal cautions about content, permissions, or follow-up actions.
